platform_claims_checked.claim: **Time:** 40 minutes total. 25 reading, 5 noting takeaways, 10 on the subagentagent primer.
Before you build multi-agent, see what a single well-shaped agent already does in the wild. Not toy demos. Working practitioners who've folded Claude Code into daily research, writing, and shipping.

1. **Simon Willison.** Browse his current [Claude Code field notes](https://simonwillison.net/tags/claude-code/). Pick one worked example where he shows the prompt, artifact, test, or correction rather than only announcing a feature.
2. **Edward Harker.** Read [How I use Claude Code](https://edwardharker.com/2026/05/16/how-i-use-claude-code/) (16 May 2026). Look for the operating routine around the agent, not a magic prompt.

5. **Daniel Bilsborough.** Read [Claude Code: The Practitioner's Guide](https://partner.danielbilsborough.com/claude-code) (updated 6 August 2026). Look for the plain-text memory and the boundary where consequential work still needs a person.
**Reading 2. Claude Code's subagentsCowork's agents, in plain language.**
Module 3 Phase 2 spawns three subagentsagents in one sessiontask. Ten minutes of orientation saves you from learning the mechanic cold in the room.
*What it is.* A subagent in Claude CodeAn agent in Cowork is a helper the main agent dispatches to do one focused job. It gets:
- access to the same **filesystem** (it reads and writes in your working directory, same as the main sessiontask).

*How to launch one.* You don't type a special command. You ask Claude, in plain language, to use one. *"Launch a subagentan agent to review the three retrieval files and write its take to `module-3/stances/planner.md`."* Claude picks it up and dispatches. To run several at once: *"Launch these three subagentsagents in parallel,"* and list them. Claude fires them together, waits for all three to return, then continues.

*What you'll see.* While a subagentan agent is working, it appears in your transcript as a running **Task** or **Agent** block (usually collapsed, with a short description of what it's doing). You can't chat with it; it's running its own conversation separately. When it finishes, the block closes with a short result, and Claude's main sessiontask picks up from there. In the Phase 2 exercise, three Task blocks will run side by side, each one writing a stance file to `module-3/stances/` as it completes.

*What you don't need.* You don't need to write an agent definition file for Module 3. You don't need to use the `/agents` slash command. Defining your own reusable subagentsagents is a later move; launching ones that the main sessiontask describes on the fly is what Phase 2 uses, and plain-language prompting is enough.

For the full reference, open Anthropic's [subagent documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents)open Claude's in-app help and search for *agents*. You're after the shape: *helper with instructions, own context, returns a result. You summon it by asking.*
